title: Minimal-privileged POC architecture notes
content:
Context:
- Customer: mid-market fintech (regulated payments) evaluating LLM assistant for dispute triage + short-response generation.
- POC timeline: 6 weeks. Budget: limited (proof-of-signal, not full scale). Data: proprietary dispute text, must stay in-region (EU).
- Primary constraints: data residency, auditability, sub-200ms median request latency for text-generation endpoint, and strict key rotation policy.

Goals for POC:
1) Demonstrate high-quality responses on a representative prompt set (precision>85% on intent classification task).
2) Show consistent latency under a 30 req/s burst profile with p95 < 350ms.
3) Prove safe data handling: data never leaves customer VPC for private option and logs masked.
4) Provide migration pathway from Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private with minimal code change.

Non-goals:
- Not optimizing token cost to minimum; focus is correctness + latency.
- Not production-grade HA for this POC (single-region is ok).

Stakeholders:
- Customer engineering lead: Elena Kovacs
- Security/compliance (customer): Martin Keller
- SE lead (Redwood): Aisha Patel
- PM: Marco Hernandez

Quick architecture options considered (summary):
A) Hosted-first (fastest to validate)
  - Redwood hosted API (region: eu-west-1), pinned model variant (quantized medium), request routing to hosted pool.
  - Pros: fastest setup, managed keys, quick telemetry.
  - Cons: data egress concerns for regulated customer, may not satisfy audit.

B) Dedicated reserved pool (Redwood Dedicated)
  - Reserved GPU pool in EU with customer-dedicated nodes, network isolation at infra-level, customer-managed KMS integration.
  - Pros: predictable throughput, better isolation, easier to set up customer key policies.
  - Cons: longer lead time (days-weeks), commit cost.

C) Private deployment (VPC connector or on-prem light package)
  - Private control plane with VPC Peering or customer-hosted inference nodes (on-prem or cloud private subnet).
  - Pros: strongest compliance posture, full data residency, can meet strict audit.
  - Cons: longest setup time, ops burden; POC may exceed timeline if on-prem required.

D) Hybrid (recommended for this POC): minimal-privileged private front with hosted/dedicated fallthrough
  - Run a small Private (VPC) gateway that accepts customer requests, performs auth, prompt pre/post-processing, and forwards inference calls to either: (1) Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 (primary), (2) Redwood hosted fallback (only if dedicated capacity exhausted and customer allows in writing).
  - Keep sensitive log masking and audit logs inside VPC. Use strict allowlist for outbound domains.
  - Why hybrid: reduces initial friction vs full private, meets data residency for primary path, allows quick recovery options for capacity during POC spikes.

Detailed hybrid proposal (minimal-privileged):
- Components to stitch:
  1) VPC Gateway (customer-managed subnet with small EC2/GKE service) running simple Redwood proxy (auth + telemetry + masking).
  2) Dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated) in eu-west-1, 2x A100-equivalent instances reserved for POC.
  3) Fallback route to hosted eu-west-1 with explicit opt-in for fallthrough (documented).
  4) KMS integration: customer key used to wrap request identifiers; Redwood only stores opaque IDs.
  5) KV cache disabled for POC (to keep behavior deterministic), but suggest enabling during post-POC perf tuning.

Traffic flow (stepwise):
- Client -> VPC Gateway (authn) -> validate/strip PII -> forward to Dedicated inference endpoint -> receive tokens -> Gateway logs masked record to S3 (in-customer-account) + sends telemetry to Redwood via audit channel (only usage counters and latency)
- If dedicated returns 503 or capacity-exceeded and customer approved fallthrough -> Gateway re-routes to Hosted endpoint flagged as FALLBACK and logs event into audit log.

Latency and capacity planning (rough numbers for POC):
- Target SLOs: median <= 200ms, p95 <= 350ms under 30 req/s burst, mean token length 40, response tokens average 80.
- Recommended instance sizing: 2 x 80GB GPU (or cloud equivalent) with batch size tuned to keep latency within SLOs.
- Expected throughput: ~12-20 req/s per node for the model class; with 2 nodes we have 24-40 req/s (meets 30 req/s target with headroom).
- Cost estimate (POC 6 weeks): Dedicated reservation (2 nodes) ~ EUR 18k + Redwood Dedicated setup fee EUR 2k + Cloud infra for gateway (small) EUR 1k. Hosted fallback pegged to pay-as-you-go if used (estimate EUR 0.06 per inference burst). These are rough and depend on exact instance types.

Security & compliance checklist for POC (minimal-privileged focus):
- Data flows documented and approved by customer security.
- Ingress only from customer-controlled IPs to VPC Gateway.
- No customer PII stored by Redwood. Logs masked at gateway.
- KMS integration for keys; key material never exported.
- Audit trail: gateway writes tamper-evident logs to customer-controlled S3 + sends hashed audit entries to Redwood (non-reversible).
- SLA exceptions: POC operates under lower SLA; customer to accept in writing.

Integration checklist (engineering tasks):
- [ ] Provision Dedicated pool ticket (JIRA: SE-5421).
- [ ] Deploy VPC Gateway template (helm chart + small NodePool).
- [ ] Implement masking middleware (open-source snippet in github: redwood-infra/poc-scripts#72).
- [ ] Connect KMS and validate key rotation.
- [ ] Create prompt test harness and evaluation set (10k prompts — subset anonymized).
- [ ] Define fallthrough policy (allowed conditions + notification list).

Risk register (POC-focused):
- Risk: Dedicated capacity lead time slips -> Mitigation: temporarily enable hosted fallback under customer-approved policy.
- Risk: Latency exceed p95 target at tail -> Mitigation: tune batch parameters, enable KV cache for warm prefixes, add third node if budget allows.
- Risk: Customer rejects any hosted fallback -> Mitigation: increase Dedicated reservation (cost) or accept longer setup for Private on-prem.
- Risk: Audit log mismatch -> Mitigation: run end-to-end audit demonstration with hashed logs and attestation.

Acceptance criteria for POC signoff:
1) Evaluation harness shows precision>=85% for intent detection and response appropriateness >= 4/5 on 100 sampled dialogs.
2) Load test demonstrates p95 <= 350ms at 30 req/s with production-like prompt distribution.
3) Security review signoff (customer compliance) on data flows and masking.
4) Migration checklist documented and demo of switching a route from Dedicated to Hosted fallback.

Next steps (immediate):
- Sync call Wed 2025-02-12 with customer security + infra to walk hybrid diagram (SOW prep).
- JIRA SE-5421: create sub-tasks for provisioning and Helm chart.
- Send proposed costs and fallback opt-in language to procurement by 2025-02-14.

Open questions / decisions needed from customer:
- Is hosted fallback acceptable under any circumstance? (yes/no)
- Will customer accept Redwood-managed Dedicated reservation or require cloud-seat under customer account?
- Any additional PII rules beyond our default masking?

Notes & working-thread logs:
- 2025-02-08: ran quick perf test on quantized-medium model locally; median 165ms on narrow prompt set (not production). Need broader test set.
- 2025-02-09: security asked to add KMS attestation step to checklist.

Appendix (quick commands and templates):
- Gateway helm deploy: repo redwood-infra/poc-scripts chart gw-quickstart values-gw-eu.yaml
- Local perf script: scripts/loadtest.py --model quantized-medium --concurrency 30 --avg-tokens 120

Comments (internal):
- Marco: "If they say no to hosted fallback we should price the full private option early — negotiating window is small."
- Riley: "Consider enabling small KV cache for high-frequency intents after week 1 to show cost improvement."
